title: FSSAI and Trademark Planning for Packaged Food Businesses in Cherthala
metaTitle: FSSAI & Trademark Guide for Cherthala Food Brands | BRNDNUR
metaDescription: Essential dual compliance guide for Cherthala packaged snack producers, coconut processors, and spice packagers. FoSCoS licensing and Trademark Classes 29 & 30.
intendedAudience: Packaged snack processors, virgin coconut oil packagers, traditional confectioners, and spice unit founders in Cherthala and Aroor taluks.
quickAnswer: Packaged food enterprises in Cherthala must secure statutory FSSAI licensing through the FoSCoS portal (Basic Registration or State License depending on annual turnover) while concurrently filing trademark applications under Class 29 (edible oils, coconut products, dairy) and Class 30 (snacks, flours, spices). This dual compliance secures food safety legality and brand ownership.

h2Sections.h2: Cherthala’s Emerging Food and Agro-Processing Industrial Belt
content: Cherthala, strategically positioned along the coastal NH 66 corridor between Kochi and Alappuzha, has transformed into a major agro-food processing and packaging center. The presence of state industrial parks, mega food parks, and abundant regional coconut plantations has encouraged entrepreneurs to launch packaged virgin coconut oil brands, vacuum-packed banana chips, organic spice mixes, and frozen culinary bases.

However, many food entrepreneurs operate under a common misconception: they believe that securing an FSSAI license grants them commercial ownership of their brand name. In reality, FSSAI only certifies food safety compliance; it confers zero legal rights to prevent a competitor in Kochi or Thrissur from registering your exact product name with the Trade Marks Registry.

callout.title: FSSAI License Does Not Grant Brand Monopoly
callout.text: FSSAI is a food hygiene license under the Food Safety and Standards Act. It does not stop competitors from copying your product name or packaging pouch. Only a registered trademark under the Trade Marks Act, 1999 guarantees brand ownership.

h2Sections.h2: Determining Your FoSCoS License Tier in Cherthala
content: Under FSSAI regulations, packaged food processing units must apply for the appropriate license tier based on capacity and annual turnover:

rows: Turnover under ₹12 Lakhs / up to 100 kg/day
Turnover ₹12 Lakhs to ₹20 Crores / up to 2 MT/day

h2Sections.h2: Nice Class Classification for Cherthala Food Products
content: Ensure your trademark application spans the correct product classes administered by the Trade Marks Registry:
checklist: Class 29 (Oils, Dairy, Processed Produce): Virgin coconut oil, copra oil, desiccated coconut flakes, processed nuts, dairy ghee, and dried seafood snacks.
Class 30 (Staples, Confectionery, Spices): Traditional chips (banana, tapioca, jackfruit), roasted flours (puttu podi, appam podi), whole and powdered spices, tea, and confectionery.
Class 31 (Raw Produce): Raw whole coconuts, unprocessed seeds, and raw agricultural commodities.
Class 35 (Retail & E-Commerce Distribution): Operating branded grocery retail outlets, supermarket concessions, and digital D2C food delivery web stores.

content: To launch your Cherthala packaged food brand compliantly without product seizures or legal disputes:

Clear your brand name on IP India, file Form TM-A with Chennai Registry using an Udyam certificate (₹4,500 government fee), submit your FoSCoS application with water potability laboratory test reports, and print retail packaging strictly complying with FSSAI (Labelling and Display) Regulations.
checklist: 1. IP India Clearance: Confirm zero phonetic conflicts in Classes 29 and 30.
2. FoSCoS Laboratory Testing: Secure water test report and food product analysis from an NABL-accredited laboratory.
3. Mandatory Label Integration: Display 14-digit FSSAI number, vegetarian green symbol, net weight, batch number, and ™ mark.
4. MSME Cost Subsidy: Use Udyam certificate to save 50% on government trademark filing fees.

faqs.question: Can I print packaging pouches in Cherthala before my trademark is fully approved?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can legally use the ™ symbol on your retail packaging as soon as Form TM-A is submitted and an official Application Number is issued by the Trade Marks Registry. However, you cannot use the registered ® symbol until the final Registration Certificate is issued.

faqs.question: Is a laboratory water test report mandatory for an FSSAI State License in Cherthala?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any commercial food manufacturing or packaging facility applying for an FSSAI State License must submit a water test report from an NABL-accredited laboratory confirming potability according to IS 10500 standards.
